title: Design Science in Information Systems Research
problem_statement: Delineating the boundaries and methodological standards of design science research in contrast to traditional behavioral research in information systems.
domain: Information Systems, Software Engineering, and Computer Science Methodology
theoretical_framework: Design Science Paradigm, Behavioral Science Paradigm, and Information Systems Research Framework
methodology: Conceptual framework synthesis and development of seven normative guidelines for artifact construction, evaluation, and communication.
evaluation: Analytical evaluation and mapping of seven foundational guidelines across exemplar design science research projects.
key_findings: Established that design science creates and evaluates IT artifacts (constructs, models, methods, instantiations) intended to solve identified organizational and technical problems.

Formulated seven core guidelines for design science research rigor: Design as an Artifact, Problem Relevance, Design Evaluation, Research Contributions, Research Rigor, Design as a Search Process, and Communication of Research.
Emphasized that empirical evaluation of artifact utility, quality, and efficiency is mandatory for establishing scientific contribution.
scope_and_delimitations: Focuses on IT and information systems artifact creation and evaluation.

limitations.verbatim_excerpt: The guidelines should be addressed in any design-science research project. However, researchers, reviewers, and editors must use their judgment to determine how and to what degree each guideline should be applied.
limitations.summary: Guidelines must be applied flexibly with domain-specific judgment rather than as a rigid bureaucratic checklist.

generalizability_gap: High-level guidelines require operationalization when applied to specific empirical deep learning benchmarks.
methodological_gap: Evaluation methods are broadly classified (observational, analytical, experimental, testing, descriptive) without specifying statistical test parameters.
future_work: Development of domain-specific evaluation metrics and formal artifact verification methods across evolving computing paradigms.
